newsitem.title: USA: Inaugural group selling thousands of ball tickets.
newsitem.headline: Inaugural group selling thousands of ball tickets.

text.p: President Clinton's inaugural committee is opening sales to the public of thousands of inaugural ball tickets, officials announced on Wednesday.

Buyers must pay $150 a ticket -- except for the youth ball, which costs $50 -- and be willing to have their names put on a list of inaugural donors to be made public after Clinton is sworn in for his second term Jan. 20.

David Seldin, deputy press secretary of the Presidential Inaugural Committee, said thousands of ball tickets would be made available to the public but he could not give an exact number. He said the committee expected to sell 70,000 to 75,000 ball tickets, including both public sales and sales to people who received invitations mailed last month.

"From the outset, our goal has been to provide as many Americans as possible with the chance to participate in this historic celebration. We are thrilled to be able to extend that effort now," Craig Smith, the inaugural committee co-executive director, said in a statement announcing the public sales.

There will be 14 inaugural balls on the evening of Jan. 20, two more than in January 1993 when Clinton took the oath of office for the first time. He plans to attend each party for at least a little while, just as he did four years ago.

Inaugural parade tickets are also going on sale but Seldin did not know how many would be available. These are tickets for a seat at bleachers being constructed along the route and will cost from $10 to $100 each. No ticket is needed for standing room.

Seldin denied the significant number of ball tickets available to the public indicated sales to invitees were not going well. "It's something we always hoped we would be able to do," he said of the public sales.

He said about 57,000 people from around the country had been invited to various inaugural events. In 1993, 400,000 people came to Washington for inaugural events including the swearing-in, the balls, the parade and a presidential gala.
To buy inaugural ball or parade tickets, the public should call 1-888-888-1997 by Saturday, and the tickets will be mailed to their homes, the inaugural committee statement said.
